claims.text: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in a single-phase solid-solution state has low hardness and strength.
Enhanced dynamic recovery during deformation causes the low hardness and strength of equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The alloy has a high stacking-fault energy.
High stacking-fault energy facilitates rapid dislocation mobility and annihilation.
Rapid dislocation mobility and annihilation limit dislocation pile-up and work hardening.
The applicable initial state is equimolar CoCrFeNiTi prepared as an as-cast and homogenized single-phase solid solution.
In situ TEM deformation testing can be used to examine dislocation generation, motion, configuration, and recovery.
The controlled comparison uses monotonic tension or compression at strain rates from 10^-4 to 10^-2 s^-1 at 25°C, 150°C, and cryogenic temperatures.
Cryogenic temperature suppresses dynamic recovery relative to room temperature and 150°C.
Dislocation density, dislocation configuration, and stacking-fault energy mediate the ease of dislocation motion.
The single-phase CoCrFeNiTi alloy contains an FCC matrix.
High stacking-fault energy in the FCC matrix promotes dynamic recovery.
Dynamic recovery reduces storage of deformation-induced defects and thereby limits work hardening, hardness, and strength.
At 25°C and 150°C, in situ TEM will reveal low net dislocation accumulation because recovery is active.
At cryogenic temperatures, the alloy will exhibit increased dislocation storage relative to its room-temperature and 150°C behavior.
Cryogenic testing will produce higher hardness and yield strength in association with increased dislocation storage.
Direct stacking-fault-energy measurements will yield high values consistent with facile dislocation motion.
Mechanical twinning may contribute under loading conditions different from those emphasized by the proposed recovery mechanism.
